meta.name: 37signals-way
meta.description: Build lean, opinionated products using the 37signals philosophy from "Getting Real", "Rework", and "Shape Up". Use when the user mentions "Getting Real", "Rework", "Shape Up", "37signals", "Basecamp method", "six-week cycles", "fixed time variable scope", "appetite vs estimates", "betting table", "breadboarding", "fat marker sketch", "build less", "underdo the competition", "opinionated software", "we have too many meetings", "how do we ship faster", or "stop overbuilding". Also trigger when cutting scope to ship sooner, running a small team, or avoiding long-term roadmaps. Covers shaping, betting, building, and the art of saying no. For MVP validation, see lean-startup. For design sprints, see design-sprint.

copy.fit_line: 适合你，如果信奉少即是多，想用固定周期和可变范围来交付产品。
copy.fit_line_en: For you if you believe in less is more and want to ship with fixed time and variable scope.

howto.what: Claude 会按照 37signals 的产品开发理念（来自《Getting Real》《Rework》《Shape Up》）来指导你。它会帮你精简功能、设定固定时间周期、组建小团队，并专注于交付真正重要的东西。
howto.when: 当你提到“Getting Real”、“Rework”、“Shape Up”、“37signals”、“Basecamp method”、“六周周期”等关键词，或者询问如何缩小范围、加快交付、管理小团队时触发。

say.text: 我们想用六周周期来开发这个新功能，该怎么开始？
功能列表太长了，怎么决定砍掉哪些？
say.note: Claude 会应用“Build Less”原则帮你筛选。

say.text: 团队只有三个人，如何高效协作？

howto.what_en: Claude will guide you using the 37signals product development philosophy (from "Getting Real", "Rework", and "Shape Up"). It helps you cut features, set fixed time cycles, run small teams, and focus on shipping what matters.
howto.when_en: Triggered when you mention keywords like "Getting Real", "Rework", "Shape Up", "37signals", "Basecamp method", "six-week cycles", or ask about cutting scope, shipping faster, or managing small teams.

say_en.text: We want to develop this feature in a six-week cycle. How do we start?
say_en.note: Claude will guide you through shaping and betting.

say_en.text: The feature list is too long. How do we decide what to cut?
say_en.note: Claude will apply the "Build Less" principle to help you trim.

say_en.text: Our team has only three people. How can we collaborate effectively?
say_en.note: Claude will recommend small-team autonomy and hill charts.
